title: Dilute graphite inclusions shorten the model ice erosion time at the proposed Gaia20cdd dust radii
abstract: We test the composition needed for small cold ice grains near the proposed warm dust of Gaia20cdd. A Maxwell-Garnett mixture and Mie heat balance update absorption and emission. For a 0.1 um grain, graphite volume fractions of 0.00198 and 0.00283 give a 61-day initial radius erosion time in the single-star 2.5 au and binary 4 au alternatives. Heating rises by factors 1.86 and 2.85 while cooling rises by less than 0.4 percent. In an ideal compact grain that retains carbon as ice leaves, these starting grains lose half their ice in 4.21 and 3.27 days. Fixed initial temperature gives half loss in about 12.5 days. These are conditional calculations, not measured abundances or grain ages. Uncertain cold-ice constants, inclusion structure, carbon retention, gas and replenishment limit the result. Code, aggregate outputs, source hashes and a retrieval recipe are included.
